comments.author: @tungtovuthanh7309

Our lovely old father, President Ho Chi Minh, said that we should welcome our enemies as friends. Only by forgiving can we continue to live happily without carrying hatred in our hearts. comments.author: @margaretadler6162
comments.text:
After visiting Vietnam many times and after spending a year and a half during the covid19 travel restrictions and seeing how the United states of America has turned a shitshow.  My wife and I sold our house,carsand just about anything we owned and moved Vietnam.  We have no regrets! 
Vietnam is a beautiful country with the most warm a friendly and amazing people in the world!  I don't ever want to live anywhere else in the world!  And certainly will not be returning to the United states! To say we love Vietnam would be understatement!  It's heaven on earth! Or as close to it as possible!

comments.author: @mikehaag907
comments.text: I was with the US Army in Vietnam in 1968-1969.  Didn't see much of any cities since our time was spent in the boonies.  But we used to say that this place would be beautiful if we didn't have a war going on.  After seeing this video, I realize how true that was!!  Amazingly gorgeous!!  Vietnam, you've done well!!

comments.author: @dug1145
comments.text: Just home from 20 days in Vietnam and Cambodia. Was an absolutely incredible experience. The food, people, city's and villages we visited were incredible. Such resilient people in both countries; who have endured so much. We were welcomed into people's homes, met survivors of S-21 and an 82-year-old Vietnamese soldier who hugged us all, and took great joy in sharing his story. Highly recommend visiting these two incredible countries.

comments.author: @kathleennichols1375
comments.text: My son lived in Vietnam for 8 years and I visited him twice. We mainly stayed in the north as he was teaching marketing at University of Hanoi. I am excited to return so I can visit the cities you reported on in your video. My son's Vietnamese fiancé's family held an elaborate engagement party in Hanoi last year. It was fascinating to learn about some of their customs.  Last month his fiancé finally got her fiancé visa and they were married in Hawaii. Now I have a beautiful Vietnamese daughter-in-law. I am tutoring her in English. She already has a good grasp of English,. it's so wonderful!

comments.author: @captainsaveaho4838
comments.text: I went to Vietnam in February of 1990. I would not recognize it now. Back then, you had to go to the local police station in every place you spent the night to show your passport and pay a very small "fee." The people were way cool to me. I believe it was about 10,000 Dong for $1 U.S. dollar. I remember all 4 of my pockets bulging out when I exchanged a $50 bill. Everything was dirt cheap. The experiences were unreal. I spent 28 interesting days going from the south to the north. Flew into Saigon and out of Hanoi to Laos. Good times

comments.author: @p0neh1
comments.text:
This video was incredibly useful for when I was planning a trip to Vietnam in late August/Early September! We also went for 10 days. Me and two of my friends went to many of the places you listed in the video. We had originally planned to go to Sapa but I decided that Hoi An was the better option for the two days instead... and it was our favourite part of the trip too! We were there on National day, so it was very busy and there were lots of festivities in Hoi An! 

We went to Ha Long for two nights instead of one, which I think was a good option as we got a whole day cruise and experience on Cat Ba Island. We also got to kayak in some very quiet and intimate areas of the bay, where nobody but the three of us could be seen or heard and discovered the most beautiful hidden gem I have ever seen. I don't usually cry but... that little part of Ha Long we kayaked into was the most beautiful place I have ever seen. We also went to Ninh Binh and spent a bit longer in Hanoi than you did - went on a couple of motorbike tours around the city and nearby countryside. It was definitely a fun experience and this video helped me decide what we would do in the short time we spent in the country!
